correctness.rationale: Expanding the qth iterate gives the vanishing of the sign polynomial at a primitive qth root. Since q is prime, the minimal polynomial is 1+X+...+X^(q−1), of the same degree as the sign polynomial; hence the signs are constant, including for points whose orbits touch the axis. The affine-rotation formula and zero mean of the roots give the obstruction for p<q/2. Otherwise the rotated half-plane normals are equally spaced, and the h-offset constraints give exactly the closed upper and open lower regular q-gons. Their centers lie strictly inside, and any noncenter has least period q since the branch rotation has order q. The map is a bijection because z↦z−H(z) translates each half-plane onto itself before the rotation. The perimeter–inradius formula gives the total area, whose strict increase over q/2<p<q gives the claimed maximum and its asymptotic. Independent tests use exact finite sign-word checks and numerical intersections of adjacent supporting lines, areas and interior orbits.
residual_risks: Replay only covers q=5,7,11; polygon and orbit checks use floating point and do not certify switching-line membership. Boundary and universal statements follow from the proof. The supplied sign-check compares equivalent coefficient predicates and is not a separate proof of the minimal-polynomial implication.
